languageModelTools.name: makerchip_compile
languageModelTools.userDescription: Compile and open TL-Verilog in Makerchip IDE.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Opens/focuses IDE and compiles TL-Verilog code. Waits up to `waitSeconds` (default 30s) for the compilation and simulation and returns a status summary on completion or timeout. By default the wait returns as soon as the compile and simulation results are ready and does NOT block on the diagram (SVG) render, which can lag or time out well after the compile finishes; set `waitForDiagram: true` to also wait for the diagram. Status includes SandPiper/Verilator exit codes, pass/fail, and a log excerpt on failure — no need to read `metadata.json` via the shell. To continue waiting, call `makerchip_wait_compile` with the returned compile ID. Set `waitSeconds` to 0 to return immediately with just the compile ID.

filePath.description: Optional path to a TL-Verilog file to open and compile. The file is read from disk (not the editor buffer). If the open buffer has unsaved edits, a warning is returned. If not provided, uses the currently active editor.

code.description: Optional TL-Verilog code to compile. When provided, creates a new unsaved file with this code and opens it in Makerchip. Use this to show examples or demonstrate TL-Verilog features.

additionalFiles.description: Optional paths to additional TL-Verilog source files to compile alongside the top file (e.g. files pulled in via m4_include). Each is read from disk and made available to the compiler under its basename, so `m4_include(['lib.tlv'])` in the top file resolves. Basenames must be unique and none may be `top.tlv` (reserved for the top file).

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`. Use this to open multiple Makerchip panels for different designs or comparisons.

waitSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for the compile to complete before returning (default 30). The tool blocks up to this long and returns a status summary. If still running when the timeout elapses, call `makerchip_wait_compile` with the returned compile ID. Set to 0 to return immediately with just the compile ID.

waitForDiagram.description: When false (default), returns as soon as the compile and simulation results are ready, without waiting for the diagram (SVG) render (which can lag or time out well after the compile finishes). Set true to also wait for the diagram, e.g. before capturing it.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_wait_compile
languageModelTools.userDescription: Wait for a Makerchip compilation to finish.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Waits for a compilation (started by makerchip_compile) to complete, then returns its status summary (SandPiper/Verilator exit codes, pass/fail, and a log excerpt on failure). By default returns as soon as the compile and simulation results are ready without blocking on the diagram (SVG) render; set `waitForDiagram: true` to also wait for the diagram. Use this to resume waiting when makerchip_compile reported the compile was still running. Blocks up to `waitSeconds` (default 30); if it is still running, call again with the same compile ID.

compileId.description: The compile ID returned by makerchip_compile.

waitSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for completion before returning (default 30). If still running, call again with the same compile ID.

waitForDiagram.description: When false (default), returns once the compile and simulation results are ready, without waiting for the diagram (SVG). Set true to also wait for the diagram, e.g. before capturing it.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_ide_call
languageModelTools.userDescription: Call any Makerchip IDE method directly.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Generic tool for calling any IDE Plugin API method directly, returning the method's result. Many of these methods are explicitly exposed as tools. Methods that return data (e.g. getKeyframe, getCode) have their return value surfaced in the tool result; a Blob return is saved to a file and its path reported. `captureVideo` is not supported here — use the dedicated `makerchip_capture_video` tool instead. For full IDE Plugin details, see `.vscode-makerchip/resources/Makerchip-public/docs/plugin_api/index.html`. Note that methods like onReady, onCodeChange, onCompilationLog are callbacks and should not be called directly.

args.description: Arguments to pass to the method. Order matters.

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_emit
languageModelTools.userDescription: Publish an application event onto the Makerchip bus.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Publish an application event onto the Makerchip application bus as the `platform.ai` participant (marking it AI-originated). Panes that subscribe to the given event `type` receive the payload (subject to their optional source filter). Use this to drive connected panes (e.g. hand a pane new input).

type.description: The application-event type to publish (e.g. 'sourceAsm'). Panes subscribe by this type.

payload.description: The event payload delivered to subscribers. Any JSON-serializable value.

target.description: Optional recipient filter (e.g. a pane mnemonic or 'ide') or an array of them. Omit to broadcast.

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_pane_call
languageModelTools.userDescription: Call a method on a connected Makerchip pane and await its result.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Call a method on a connected third-party pane and await its result (host-to-pane RPC). This is the request/response complement to makerchip_emit's fire-and-forget broadcast: use it when you need a value back from a pane you opened (e.g. tell the Compiler Explorer pane to run and wait for the outcome). The pane must have opened with `rpc: true` and implement a handler for the named method. Name the pane by its (uniquified) mnemonic.

mnemonic.description: The target pane's mnemonic (as returned when opening/reserving a third-party pane).

method.description: The pane method to invoke. The pane must have declared `rpc: true` and implement this method.

args.description: Positional arguments passed to the pane method. Any JSON-serializable values.

timeoutMs.description: Optional response timeout in milliseconds. Default: 30000.

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_get_viz_image
languageModelTools.userDescription: Capture the current VIZ visualization as an image.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Captures the current Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) view canvas (resulting from compiled/simulated code) and returns it inline as an image for the agent to inspect — use this to iterate on VIZ development and video rendering. It can also return the current view's absolute camera keyframe (scale/focus/size) for reuse in makerchip_capture_video; one call can return the image, the keyframe, or both. The image can additionally be saved to a file for the user, or captured for the user only (skipping the inline image to spend no vision tokens).

quality.description: Image quality for jpeg/webp formats (0.0-1.0). Default is 1.0.

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

saveToFile.description: Optional: also save the image to a file for the user to view. If true, saves to a temp file with an auto-generated name; if a string, uses it as the file path. (The image is also returned inline to the model unless `blind` is set.)

blind.description: When true, do not return the image to the model — capture it to a file only, for the user. Spends no vision tokens. A file is always written (auto-named in the temp dir unless `saveToFile` gives a path).

response.description: What to return. 'both' (default) captures the image AND the current view's absolute keyframe; 'image' returns only the image; 'keyframe' returns only the keyframe (no image render — cheap). The keyframe is {cycle, scale, focus:{x,y}, width, height}, ready to drop into makerchip_capture_video's `keyframes` with `absolute: true`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_extract_pdf_figure
languageModelTools.userDescription: Extract a figure's vector geometry and text labels from a PDF page (for Live Doc VIZ authoring).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Extracts a figure's vector geometry (SVG-path primitives) and text labels from a PDF page, for authoring and debugging Makerchip Live Doc `\viz_js` code. Runs the SAME `this.global.pdf.extractFigure` that Live Doc code uses at runtime, INSIDE an open Makerchip IDE panel, so the returned coordinates, labels, cluster selection, figure bbox and coordinate transforms match EXACTLY what a VIZ overlay will see (no drift). Requires an open Makerchip panel; does NOT require a compiled design. Use this to inspect a PDF before writing Live Doc overlays: find label positions to anchor to, choose a `select` mode / cluster index, and read the coordinate `transforms`. Returns the ExtractResult JSON `{primitives, labels, space, figure, bbox, page, transforms, meta}`; SVG path `d` strings are omitted by default (set includePaths=true to include them). No copy of the figure is produced — geometry is re-derived from the referenced PDF. See the Live Doc API skill/docs for the full authoring API (`extractFigure`, `toFabric`, `buildFigure`).

source.description: PDF source: a URL to the PDF, reachable from the Makerchip IDE (resolved through its CORS proxy, like \viz_js code).

select.description: Figure-selection descriptor. Modes: {mode:"largest"} (default, densest cluster); {mode:"cluster", index} (nth-densest, 0-based); {mode:"clusterAt", at:[x,y], space} (cluster at/nearest a point); {mode:"region", rect:[x0,y0,x1,y1], space} (explicit crop); {mode:"all"} (whole page). `space` for at/rect is "pdf" (default), "device", or "norm".

gap.description: Cluster-join distance in device px. Default: 12.

space.description: Output coordinate space. Default: "figure" (figure top-left at origin).

text.description: Which text to return: "labels" (default, inside the figure), "all", or "none".

clip.description: Clip primitives to the figure bounds: true (pad 4px), a number (explicit pad px), or omit for no clip.

includePaths.description: Include the SVG path `d` string on each primitive. Default false (omitted to keep the result compact). Set true only if you need the exact vector paths.

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_capture_video
languageModelTools.userDescription: Capture the VIZ simulation across a cycle range as a GIF, MP4, WebM, or APNG video.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Captures the Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) canvas across a range of simulation cycles and encodes it as a video, from an open IDE panel with compiled/simulated code. Use this to produce an animation of a design's behavior over time. Beyond the plain cycle range, it can capture intra-cycle animation, set playback speed, animate a camera pan/zoom, record at a fixed resolution/aspect, and emit GIF, MP4, WebM, or APNG. The result is always written to a file (auto-named in the temp dir unless you pass `filename`) and the path is returned; for image formats (GIF/APNG) you can then view that file to inspect the frame(s). TIP: to calibrate camera framing before a full render, call `makerchip_get_viz_image` (default `response: "both"`) to see the current view and get it as an absolute keyframe in one step, then derive your keyframes from that (with `absolute: true`) instead of rendering a throwaway clip. The user can also position the view for you to capture.

format.description: Output format. 'auto' (default) lets the IDE choose: GIF for one frame per cycle, MP4 otherwise. Set explicitly to force a codec (e.g. 'mp4' for a shareable video, 'webm' for VP9, 'gif'/'apng' for looping clips). Independent of the output `filename` and its extension.

fps.description: Output frames per second. Omit for one frame per cycle (settled final state, no intra-cycle animation).

cyclesPerSecond.description: Playback speed in simulation cycles per second. Default: 1 (one cycle per second); e.g. 20 plays each cycle for 50ms.

Mbps.description: Video bitrate in Mbps (MP4 output; ignored for GIF). Default: 2.5 (recommended 10 for high quality).

width.description: Recording width in pixels. Defaults to the live VIZ pane canvas width. Set this together with height to record at a fixed resolution/aspect independent of the pane size (rendered headless in an offscreen canvas).

height.description: Recording height in pixels. Defaults to the live VIZ pane canvas height. Set this together with width to record at a fixed resolution/aspect independent of the pane size.

backgroundColor.description: CSS canvas background color (e.g. 'white' or '#1e1e1e'). Defaults to the VIZ default.

timeout.description: Override the automatically computed RPC timeout, in seconds (capped at 3600). Only needed when a capture legitimately runs slower than the estimate allows; supplying it also bypasses the automatic refusal of large jobs. WARNING: encoding buffers every rendered frame in memory (ffmpeg via WebAssembly), so a long timeout with many/high-resolution frames can exhaust the webview heap and crash it — prefer reducing the cycle range, fps, or resolution over raising this.

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

filename.description: Optional output file path. If omitted, a timestamped file is written to the OS temp dir. The video is always saved to a file (never inlined into the conversation).

keyframes.description: Camera keyframes for pan/zoom motion across the cycle range. A single keyframe = static camera; multiple keyframes animate the camera (Catmull-Rom interpolated). In relative mode (default) `scale` is a multiplier on the current VIZ scale (2 = 2x zoom in, 0.5 = zoom out) and `focus` is an {x,y} offset as a fraction of the visible area (+x right, +y down); here keyframes may be OMITTED for no camera motion (records the current view). In absolute mode (see `absolute`) `scale`/`focus` are absolute VIZ scale/coordinates, the current view is not used, and keyframes are REQUIRED (at least one entry) — `default` only fills in properties an entry omits, it does not replace the array.

cycle.description: Cycle at which this keyframe applies. First/last default to startCyc/endCyc when omitted.

scale.description: Camera zoom (relative multiplier, or absolute pixels to canvas units when `absolute` is true).

focus.description: Camera center (relative fractional offset, or absolute VIZ coordinate when `absolute` is true).

width.description: Absolute mode only. Canvas width (px) that this keyframe's absolute `scale` was measured against — i.e. the `width` from `getKeyframe`. The recorder rescales `scale` by min(recordingWidth/width, recordingHeight/height) so the same framing holds when recording at a different resolution. Omit to assume the recording width (or `default.width`). Does not affect `focus`, which is a size-independent absolute coordinate.

height.description: Absolute mode only. Canvas height (px) that this keyframe's absolute `scale` was measured against — the `height` from `getKeyframe` (see `width`). Omit to assume the recording height (or `default.height`).

absolute.description: When true, keyframe `scale`/`focus` are absolute VIZ scale/coordinates rather than relative to the current view (good for reproducibility); get the current view as an absolute keyframe from `makerchip_get_viz_image`. Defaults to `false`, where keyframes are relative to the current view (good for building on a view the user has positioned).

default.description: Default values for any keyframe property except `cycle` (same shape as a `keyframes` entry — e.g. `scale`, `focus`, `width`, `height`). (Often `{width, height}`.) Supplies these to any keyframe that omits them; a keyframe's own value takes precedence. Does not remove the requirement to pass at least one `keyframes` entry in absolute mode.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_get_layout_state
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get the current IDE pane layout configuration.
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Retrieves the current Makerchip IDE layout state as a serializable object from an open IDE panel. The returned data structure refects the recursive binary tree of splits and the tabbed panes at leaf splits, identified by their mnemonics.

Use this to: capture current layout for later restoration, understand current IDE configuration, or create modified layouts based on the current state. The returned object can be passed directly to makerchip_set_layout_state or modified before restoration.

SEE: `.vscode-makerchip/.vscode/skills/makerchip-api-features.md` for details about working with layouts and panes

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_set_layout_state
languageModelTools.userDescription: Configure the IDE pane layout (create splits, arrange panes in tabs, set active pane).

state.description: Layout state defining pane arrangement (TabbedView or FlexSplit)

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

panes.description: Array of pane mnemonics in tab order

oneOf.description: Horizontal split with left and right sides
Vertical split with top and bottom sides

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_get_available_panes
languageModelTools.userDescription: List all available IDE panes with descriptions.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns all panes with mnemonics (name[+uniquifier]), display names, descriptions, and availability. Main panes: Log, Nav-TLV, Diagram, Viz, Waveform. Static panes: Tutorials, Examples, Courses. Third-party panes if any. Only use panes with available=true in layout operations.

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_open_pane
languageModelTools.userDescription: Open or activate a specific IDE pane by mnemonic.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Opens and/or activates a pane by mnemonic in an open IDE panel. Works with static panes (Tutorials, Examples, opened on demand), main panes (Log, Diagram, etc.), and third-party panes. Use makerchip_get_available_panes for valid mnemonics. For complex layouts use makerchip_set_layout_state.

mnemonic.description: The mnemonic (unique identifier) of the pane to open or activate. Use makerchip_get_available_panes to discover valid mnemonics.

background.description: If true, opens the pane in the background without activating it. Default is false (activate the pane).

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_fit_pane
languageModelTools.userDescription: Fit a pane's content to its viewport (zoom to fit).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Sends a 'fit content' request to the pane with the given mnemonic. It is up to the pane whether it acts: VIZ and Diagram fit their scalable content to the viewport (equivalent to the Reset Zoom control), Waveform zooms to the full time range (Zoom Full), and other panes ignore the request. Returns whether the pane acted; success defaults to false when the pane is not found or does not support fitting. Use makerchip_get_available_panes for valid mnemonics.

mnemonic.description: The mnemonic (unique identifier) of the pane to fit (e.g. 'Viz', 'Diagram', 'Waveform'). Use makerchip_get_available_panes to discover valid mnemonics.

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_open_third_party_pane
languageModelTools.userDescription: Open custom content (PDFs, web pages) in IDE panes.

mnemonic.description: Display name for the pane (tab label). Will be uniquified automatically if a pane with this name already exists.

contentType.description: Type of content to display: 'pdf' for PDF viewer or 'iframe' for embedded web content.

contentUrl.description: URL to the content. For PDFs: supports https://, http://, file://, vscode-webview://, data URIs. For iframes: must support iframe embedding. Provide this OR filePath.

filePath.description: Absolute path to a local file to load. The extension reads the file and builds a data: URI internally, so large file contents never pass through the model context. Preferred over contentUrl for local files. Takes precedence when both are provided.

contentParams.description: Content parameters. Provide either contentUrl or filePath.

background.description: If true, opens the pane without activating it (leaves current pane active). Default is false.

nonTransferrable.description: If true, pane construction data won't be stored for layout recovery. Use for temporary panes. Default is false.

channel.description: Optional channel contract wiring this pane onto the IDE communication bus. Enables connected multi-pane flows where one pane's events drive another (e.g. Compiler Explorer producing `sourceAsm` consumed by a WARP-V pane).

produces.description: Event types this pane may publish on the bus (e.g. ["sourceAsm"]).

subscribes.description: Event types this pane receives, optionally scoped to specific source agents.

sources.description: Source agent identities to accept this event from (e.g. the mnemonic of the producing pane, or "ide").

rpc.description: If true, the pane may issue bounded IDE RPC calls (whitelisted safe Plugin API operations).

params.description: Optional opaque parameters delivered to the pane via its `getContext` RPC. Shape is pane-defined (e.g. Compiler Explorer expects `{"ce": {"language", "compiler", "options", "filters", "source"}}`).

panelName.description: Optional VS Code panel name to target. Default: `default`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_get_late_reply
languageModelTools.userDescription: Retrieve an IDE reply that arrived after its call timed out.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the most recent IDE reply that arrived after its call had already timed out (with method, requestId, kind, value, timestamp), or nothing if none. Only use this when a timeout error explicitly refers you to it.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_get_cycle
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get the active cycle/time step.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns active cycle value. All "live" panes (Nav-TLV, Diagram, VIZ, Waveform) display data for this cycle. Cycle 0 is first cycle after reset.

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_set_cycle
languageModelTools.userDescription: Set the active cycle/time step.

cycle.description: Absolute cycle to jump to (0-based). Mutually exclusive with offset. Final value clamped to [0, endCycle].

offset.description: Relative offset from current cycle (can be negative). Mutually exclusive with cycle.

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_update_play_state
languageModelTools.userDescription: Start or stop waveform playback animation.
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Controls waveform playback animation (cycle advancement). Starts or stops playback, optionally setting cycle range and playback speed.

When starting (isPlaying=true):
- Advances active cycle automatically at specified interval (cycleTimeout, default 1000ms)
- Optionally jumps to startCyc before starting
- Stops at endCyc if provided, otherwise plays to end of waveform
- Updates all live panes (Nav-TLV, Diagram, VIZ, Waveform) each cycle

When stopping (isPlaying=false):
- Stops cycle advancement at current position
- Other parameters ignored

EXAMPLES:
- Start playback from beginning at 500ms/cycle: {"isPlaying": true, "cycleTimeout": 500, "startCyc": 0}
- Play cycles 10-50 at default speed: {"isPlaying": true, "startCyc": 10, "endCyc": 50}
- Stop playback: {"isPlaying": false}

isPlaying.description: Whether to start (true) or stop (false) waveform playback.

cycleTimeout.description: Delay in milliseconds between cycles during playback. Default is 1000ms. Only used when isPlaying=true.

startCyc.description: Starting cycle for playback. If provided, jumps to this cycle before starting. Only used when isPlaying=true.

endCyc.description: Ending cycle for playback. If provided, playback stops at this cycle; otherwise plays to end of waveform. Only used when isPlaying=true.

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_highlight
languageModelTools.userDescription: Highlight a signal, scope, or pipeline stage across all IDE views.
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Highlights all replicated instances of an entity across the IDE (Nav-TLV, Diagram, Waveform). If accumulate=false (default), replaces highlights. If true, adds to existing.

PATH SYNTAX (varies by type):
- Pipesignal: '/cpu|pipe$data' (full path)
- Scope: '/cpu', '/core|in/flit', or '/unit|reg' (full path)
- Stage: '|pipe@2' (not a full path; just pipeline and pipestage)

Never include range/index expressions, like `[2]`.
NEVER include M5 macros or `\TLV` macro parameters, like `|inst\m5_cnt` or `|_pipe`.

EXAMPLES: {"id": "/cpu|decode$valid"}, {"id": "|fetch@1", "accumulate": true}

id.description: The TL-Verilog path identifier to highlight (e.g., '/cpu|my_pipe$data', '|my_pipe@2', '/cpu')

accumulate.description: If true, adds to existing highlights (Ctrl+click behavior). If false (default), replaces all highlights.

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_clear_highlights
languageModelTools.userDescription: Clear all highlighted entities from IDE views.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Removes all entity highlights from all views: Diagram, Waveform, Nav-TLV panes.

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_set_dark_mode
languageModelTools.userDescription: Enable or disable dark mode in the Makerchip IDE.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Controls dark/light theme for all IDE views (editor, diagram, waveform). Pass true for dark mode, false for light mode. Updates localStorage and all panes immediately.

enabled.description: Enable dark mode (true) or light mode (false).

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_set_live_mode
languageModelTools.userDescription: Enable or disable live mode for a specific pane (Diagram, Nav-TLV).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Controls live/dead mode for panes that support it. Live panes auto-update as cycle changes during playback/stepping. Dead panes freeze at current cycle. Supported: Diagram, Nav-TLV. VIZ is always live. Returns true if successful, false if pane not found or doesn't support live mode.

mnemonic.description: The mnemonic of the pane to control (e.g., 'Diagram', 'Nav-TLV').

enabled.description: Enable live mode (true) or dead mode/freeze (false).

panelName.description: Optional panel name to target. Default: `default`.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_list_panels
languageModelTools.userDescription: List all currently open Makerchip IDE panels.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns open panel names. Use these in 'panelName' parameter to target specific IDE instances. New panels are created only via makerchip_compile with a code or filePath argument.

languageModelTools.name: makerchip_reload_panels
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reload open Makerchip panels, reconnecting to the current server/tunnel.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reloads every open Makerchip panel against the freshly-resolved Makerchip server/tunnel URL (from the ACTIVE_TUNNELS registry or makerchip.serverUrl). Use to recover already-open panels after a restart: the sandserv backend was restarted (dropped connections), or a dev tunnel was recreated by `./launch :port` (new URL after the old one died). Lighter than reloading the whole window; takes no parameters and affects all open panels.
